newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 16.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* A government report showed U.S. consumer prices in March rose one-tenth of one percent, easing some inflation concerns.
* The Dow Jones industrials roared higher, closing up 135.26 points at 6,587.16, although Nasdaq ended lower.
* Both Chase Manhattan and Citicorp reported results that were ahead of analyst forecasts but said credit card losses had hampered earnings.
* Merrill Lynch and PaineWebber posted strong earnings, helped by gains in investment banking and asset management, but Salomon Inc's earnings declined 37 percent due to bond market pressures.
* Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer posted earnings gains of more than 10 percent on strong new drug sales.
* Ameritech, GTE and Sprint earnings met or beat forecasts, helped by strength in core telephone businesses and enhanced services.

* Columbia/HCA and Value Health Inc revised financial terms of their proposed merger to compensate for Columbia/HCA's recent stock price decline. Under new terms, Columbia/HCA would pay about $1.12 billion in cash.
* Eastman Kodak reported lower earnings in the first quarter, as expected.
* Two top U.S. trade negotiators with China, Lee Sands and Deborah Lehr, said they were resigning.
* Midwestern U.S. insurance company Guarantee Trust Life Insurance said it was starting to offer life insurance to some people who were HIV positive.
* Market Place: Felix Rohatyn, just nominated U.S. Ambassador to France, could leave Lazard Freres, raising questions about how the firm would look if he goes.
* Large bond firms like Bear Stearns, Goldman, Sachs and PaineWebber are still contributing heavily to U.S. political campaigns despite a rule designed to restrict such gifts.
* Insider trading seems to have returned to Wall Street, with National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) regulators finding suspicious trading activity almost daily.
